record.original_question: For two-armed Bernoulli bandits in the fixed-budget setting, Kaufmann et al. (2016) show that an optimal sampling vector exists, but that vector depends on the unknown means of the two arms and therefore is not available a priori. Is there an algorithm that can still achieve asymptotic optimality in this setting without requiring prior knowledge of those unknown arm means?

evidence.quote: However, for two-armed Bernoulli bandits, Kaufmann et al. (2016) shows that though the optimal sampling vector exists, it requires the knowledge of unknown means of the arms, which is unknown a priori. It is unclear whether there is an algorithm can achieve the asymptotic optimality without such a requirement.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the fixed-budget best-arm identification problem for two-armed Bernoulli bandits. There are two arms with unknown means $\mu_1, \mu_2 \in (0,1)$, $\mu_1 \neq \mu_2$, and an algorithm is given a total budget of $T$ samples. At each round $t = 1, \dots, T$, the algorithm chooses an arm $A_t \in \{1,2\}$ (based on past observations) and observes an independent reward $X_t \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(\mu_{A_t})$. After $T$ rounds, the algorithm outputs a recommended arm $\hat{a}_T$, and its error probability is $p_T(\mu_1,\mu_2) = \Pr(\hat{a}_T \neq \arg\max_i \mu_i)$.

It is known that, for each instance $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$, there exists an optimal (instance-dependent) sampling proportion $w^*(\mu_1,\mu_2) \in (0,1)$ characterizing the best achievable asymptotic exponential decay rate
$$\Gamma^*(\mu_1,\mu_2) = -\lim_{T\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{T}\log p_T(\mu_1,\mu_2),$$
but $w^*$ depends on the unknown means.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm, not having prior knowledge of $\mu_1,\mu_2$, that is asymptotically optimal in the sense that
$$-\liminf_{T\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{T}\log p_T(\mu_1,\mu_2) \geq \Gamma^*(\mu_1,\mu_2)$$
for every instance $(\mu_1,\mu_2)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on universally optimal algorithms for A/B testing (Adusumilli, "On Universally Optimal Algorithms for A/B Testing," arXiv:2308.12000) addresses this question for two-armed Bernoulli bandits in fixed budget. It establishes that uniform sampling is universally asymptotically optimal: no algorithm in the natural class of consistent and stable algorithms can strictly outperform uniform sampling on any instance while matching it elsewhere. Thus uniform allocation—which requires no knowledge of the unknown means—achieves the asymptotic optimal rate for two-armed Bernoulli bandits.

status_evidence.title: On Universally Optimal Algorithms for A/B Testing
status_evidence.snippet: there is no algorithm better than the uniform sampling algorithm ... answers an open problem posed by Qin (2022) definitively: the uniform sampling strategy—which equally allocates budget between the two arms without learning their means—is universally optimal in an asymptotic sense.
status_evidence.claim: Uniform sampling, which does not require knowledge of the arm means, achieves asymptotic optimality for two-armed Bernoulli bandit fixed-budget best-arm identification.

status_evidence.title: Minimax Optimal Simple Regret in Two-Armed Best-Arm Identification
status_evidence.snippet: Neyman allocation reduces to uniform allocation under Bernoulli distributions and is asymptotically optimal.
status_evidence.claim: For two-armed Bernoulli problems, the optimal allocation coincides with uniform allocation, which requires no knowledge of the means.
